Description: Reva authorization interceptor for an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway: the interceptor Lambda function, its DynamoDB trace-history table (reva_trace_hop), the RTG token secret (reva/secrets, created with the placeholder value abc: edit it to the real token) and its IAM role. Attach the function to your gateway as a REQUEST interceptor (see the stack outputs).

Label.default: Interceptor code (a zip in S3, in this region)
Resources this stack creates (change a name only if it clashes)

CodeS3Bucket.default: S3 bucket holding the interceptor zip

CodeS3Key.default: S3 key of the interceptor zip

HistoryTableName.default: Name of the DynamoDB history table

TokenSecretName.default: Name of the Secrets Manager secret for the RTG token

TokenSecretKey.default: Field of the secret that holds the token

RtgAuthMode.default: How the RTG token is sent

PromptKey.default: Prompt field name in the RTG request

UserClaim.default: JWT claim that identifies the user

AuthorizeAgent.default: Use the calling agent as the subject

FailOpen.default: Let calls through when the RTG is unreachable

MonitorMode.default: Monitor only: log denials but allow

GatewayServiceRoleName.default: Name of the gateway's service role

CodeS3Bucket.Description: S3 bucket, in the same region as this stack, that holds the interceptor zip (handler.py and the interceptor/ folder at the top of the zip). Build it with: zip -r interceptor.zip handler.py interceptor -x "*__pycache__*"

CodeS3Key.Description: S3 key of the interceptor zip. Use a new key for each version you deploy: CloudFormation only updates the function when the key changes.

HistoryTableName.Description: Name of the DynamoDB table this stack creates for the per-trace hop history. A table with this name must not already exist in this region; change it if one does, or if you deploy the stack twice in the same region.
HistoryTableName.ConstraintDescription: 3 to 255 characters: letters, numbers, underscore, hyphen and dot

TokenSecretName.Description: Name of the Secrets Manager secret this stack creates for the Reva RTG token. It is created with the placeholder value abc: edit the value after the stack is created (see the TokenSecretArn output). A secret with this name must not already exist in this region.

TokenSecretKey.Description: The field of the secret's JSON that holds the token. The secret is created as {"RTG_TOKEN": "abc"}; keep this field name when you edit the value.

RtgBaseUrl.Description: Base URL of the Reva RTG. The evaluation path is added by the function.
RtgBaseUrl.ConstraintDescription: Must start with https:// (or http:// for local testing)

RtgAuthMode.Description: api-token sends the token as X-API-Token; bearer sends it as Authorization: Bearer.

PromptKey.Description: Name of the prompt field in the RTG request (older policy stores use content).

UserClaim.Description: JWT claim that identifies the user (the principal).

AuthorizeAgent.Description: true: an agent that identifies itself (token claim act.sub or the X-Reva-Agent-Id header) is the subject; false: the user is the subject on every hop.

TargetsJson.Description: JSON object that renames or excludes gateway targets, for example {"my-tools": {"id": "my-mcp"}}. {} for none.

ContextMapJson.Description: JSON object that maps a call's argument names to the Cedar context attributes your policies read, for example {"countries": "Acme_req_countries"}. {} for none.

FailOpen.Description: true lets calls through when the RTG or the history table is unreachable. false (recommended) denies them. Policy denials are never let through.

MonitorMode.Description: true logs what the RTG would deny but lets the call through. Useful for a first run; nothing is blocked while it is true.

DebugLogging.Description: true logs the event shape and the RTG request, which contains prompts. Development only.

FunctionTimeout.Description: Function timeout in seconds. Keep it well above the 15 second RTG call timeout.

LogRetentionDays.Description: Days to keep the function's CloudWatch logs.

GatewayServiceRoleName.Description: Optional. Name (not ARN) of your gateway's service role. When set, this stack adds the lambda:InvokeFunction permission on the interceptor to that role. Leave empty to add the permission yourself.

Properties.Description: Reva RTG token for the AgentCore Gateway interceptor. Created with the placeholder value abc: edit the value to the real token (Secrets Manager, Retrieve secret value, Edit).
Execution role of the Reva AgentCore Gateway interceptor: logs, the trace-history table and the RTG token secret.
Asks the Reva RTG whether each AgentCore Gateway request is allowed before it is forwarded.

InterceptorFunctionArn.Description: ARN of the interceptor function. Attach it to your gateway as a REQUEST interceptor.

InterceptorConfiguration.Description: Save as interceptors.json and pass it to the gateway: aws bedrock-agentcore-control update-gateway --gateway-identifier <id> --interceptor-configurations file://interceptors.json (plus the gateway's other required parameters).

TableName.Description: DynamoDB table that holds the per-trace hop history.

TokenSecretArn.Description: The secret created for the RTG token. It holds the placeholder value abc: set the real token before use (Secrets Manager, open the secret, Retrieve secret value, Edit; keep the field name RTG_TOKEN). The function picks up a new value within 5 minutes.

ExecutionRoleArn.Description: Execution role of the interceptor function.

LogGroupName.Description: CloudWatch log group of the interceptor function. Each evaluated call logs one decision line.

GatewayInvokePermission.Description: Whether this stack gave your gateway's service role permission to invoke the interceptor.

Fn::If: Not added: allow lambda:InvokeFunction on the interceptor for your gateway's service role, or set GatewayServiceRoleName
